newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares trade sideways as bourse trade opens.
newsitem.headline: German shares trade sideways as bourse trade opens.

text.p: A quiet start to German share trade on Monday, with the market expected to tread water over the day as the U.S. Labor Day holiday scuppered hopes of the DAX finding any new direction.
In early bourse trade the DAX index, which gauges trade in 30 German blue-chip stocks, was down 6.45 points, or 0.25 percent, at 2,537.38 points.

A slightly firmer dollar helped offset the effect of lower German bonds, but the U.S. currency was still way off its highs of several weeks ago and did not provide any real inspiration in trade generally lacking direction.
Carmaker Volkswagen AG was hit by early selling following a newspaper report on Friday of problems with cars produced at its Wolfsburg plant.
Volkswagen was down four marks at 546 marks early on.
Shares in mixed utility Veba AG were boosted at bourse open by reports that it was planning a deal with gas company Ruhrgas on use of Ruhrgas' cable network for Veba's telecoms business.
Veba shares later traded 15 pfennigs lower at 77.50 marks in line with the market.
German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG was three marks lower at 207.50 marks after German cartel authorities confirmed they were looking into its pricing structure on domestic flights.
